item.title: Black hole binary mergers in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity with regularisation
item.description: We study the non-linear dynamics of Chern-Simons gravity with numerical relativity for the first time. We use the regularisation prescription to obtain a well-posed initial-value formulation in the gauges commonly used in numerical relativity, and we simulate head-on collisions and binary black hole mergers in the regime of validity of effective field theory, extracting the corresponding scalar and gravitational waves. This opens up the possibility to test general effective field theories of gravity, including those with higher-than-second-order equations of motion, with gravitational waves. — Llibert Arest\'e Sal\'o, Maxence Corman, Pau Figueras, \'Aron D. Kov\'acs, Shunhui Yao — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Rotating black hole thermodynamics at NNLO in higher-curvature gravity
item.description: We investigate higher-curvature corrections to black-hole thermodynamics in quasitopological gravity using perturbative Euclidean-action methods. Static, spherically symmetric black holes provide a benchmark for the action expansion, while our main application concerns five-dimensional, asymptotically flat, rotating black holes with equal angular momenta. For Einstein gravity supplemented by Gauss--Bonnet and cubic quasitopological interactions, we compute the Gibbs free energy through next-to-next-to-leading order, retaining both quadratic and cubic corrections. item.title: Melvin-type Electromagnetized Kerr Black Hole in Kaluza-Klein and Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion Theories
item.description: A naive application of solution-generating techniques to construct Melvin-type rotating black holes in the Kaluza-Klein (KK) theory in the presence of both electric and magnetic external fields generically introduces an undesirable Taub-swirling twist term. We investigate its origin and modify the electromagnetization procedure, thereby constructing an exact solution of the Melvin-type electromagnetized Kerr black hole in the KK theory without the swirling term. We also obtain the analogous solution in the Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion (EMDA) theory. The modified solution-generating techniques allow one to introduce both the dyonic charges and external electromagnetic fields independently… — Liang Ma, Zhi-Chao Li, H. item.title: Surrogate Modeling and Reduced-Order Methods in Gravitational-Wave Physics and Numerical Relativity: From Spectral Representations to Adaptive Compression
item.description: The rapid expansion of gravitational-wave astronomy and high-precision numerical relativity has created an acute computational bottleneck: direct numerical integration of the Einstein field equations and high-dimensional Bayesian parameter estimation require millions of waveform evaluations that cannot be sustained by traditional solvers alone. Reduced-order modeling (ROM) and surrogate techniques have emerged as foundational tools to bridge this gap, compressing high-fidelity solution manifolds into compact, rapidly evaluable representations without sacrificing physical accuracy. item.title: Comment on "Exact, nonsingular black holes from a phantom DBI field as primordial dark matter"
item.description: We demonstrate that the metric and scalar configuration proposed in Ref.~[1] do not satisfy the complete set of field equations of the Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) field theory minimally coupled to general relativity on a radial domain containing the event horizon. The physical DBI branch for this gravitational setup terminates outside the event horizon. Thus, the proposed configuration does not describe a black hole solution of that theory. — Mustapha Azreg-A\"{i}nou, Marco A. A. de Paula — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Holography at finite resolution: zero-point length in AdS/CFT
item.description: We explore the zero-point length $l_0$ of T-duality-inspired effective field theory in holography, distinguishing two readings. As a boundary resolution scale, $l_0$ filters the source of a bulk scalar in anti-de Sitter space and yields an exactly solvable boundary response that is ultraviolet finite without a hard cutoff and inherits the power-law tails of the zero-point-length kernel. We show that this filter is the source-normalized bulk-to-boundary transfer function of a $\nu=1$ scalar evaluated at radial depth $z=l_0$. Anchoring Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces on the same radial surface gives finite entanglement entropies that retain the perimeter law and the universal sphere free energy. item.title: Boundary preparation and anomalous relaxation near a black hole exceptional point
item.description: We study the relaxation of a Robin scalar field near a stable exceptional point of a planar Schwarzschild AdS black hole, where finite boundary driving controls the recovery time without changing the leading decay rate at linear order. At the exceptional point, two weighted moments of the source determine the time dependence of the leading response. When the zeroth moment vanishes while the first remains nonzero, the linear time factor is eliminated, leaving an ordinary exponential decay. With suitable boundary preparation, a perturbation that retains more energy at release can nevertheless reach a common recovery threshold sooner. item.title: An energy-dependent rescaling of the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian: Standard Model Extension identification, matter sector, and long-baseline degeneracy
item.description: We study the consequences of multiplying the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian by a real, energy-dependent scalar, $H_\eta(E)=f(E)H_0(E)$ with $f(E)=1-\eta_0(E/E_0)^2$, a minimal-length ansatz. The matter-potential rescaling has dimension-five behaviour and is CPT-odd. item.title: ER=EPR and IMP wormholes in quantum gravity
item.description: We analyze and refine the ER=EPR conjecture by studying IMP (Isenberg, Mazzeo and Pollack \cite{Isenberg:2001qe}) wormholes in QFT and quantum gravity, in the AdS/CFT context. IMP wormholes are solutions to the Einstein equations constructed from another general solution of Einstein's equations by gluing a handle on a Cauchy slice with a constant mean curvature, so that the initial data on the slice does not change in the regions away from the handle. This is made possible by using what is called the conformal method. This same method also enables one to recover a well defined perturbation theory in quantum gravity, and particularly for asymptotically AdS spacetimes \cite{Witten:2022xxp}… — Eyoab Bahiru — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Orbit-averaged spinning and eccentric binary black holes: Hamiltonian and integrability
item.description: For over two decades, the orbit-averaged precession equations of spinning binary black holes at second post-Newtonian order have been a standard model for their spin dynamics. One of their constants of motion, the projected effective spin, underlies the stability analysis of aligned-spin configurations and the construction of analytical solutions. The system is known to be Hamiltonian and integrable, its Hamiltonian being the orbit average of the full post-Newtonian Hamiltonian. Independently, we derive this Hamiltonian from the equations of motion alone, show why the orbit average gives the correct equations, and relate its constants of motion to those of the full system. item.description: The discovery potential for heavy charged Higgs bosons $H^\pm$ decaying into a top-bottom quark pair is investigated at a future $e^+e^-$ collider operating at $\sqrt{s}=1.4~\mathrm{TeV}$. The study considers charged Higgs masses between 200 and 600 GeV within all four Yukawa types of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). The boosted $tb$ final state is explored using complementary cut-based and machine-learning analyses based on boosted decision trees (BDT). item.title: Finite regularity moduli stacks through diffeology
item.description: Diffeological non-Abelian Hodge theory motivates the study of $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and flat bundles for finite $r$. As an application, we construct moduli stacks over the sites of $C^r$ manifolds parametrizing $C^r$ vector bundles over a smooth manifold, and $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and of flat bundles over a complex manifold. item.title: Light fermions can trigger a Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
item.description: The Brout-Englert-Higgs effect produces the masses of the Standard Model particles. However, the cause of this effect is unknown. Beyond-the-Standard-Model theories aim to find the source of this effect, for example using a composite Higgs and dynamically generating its vacuum expectation value. In this paper, we show evidence from lattice simulations with vectorially coupled fermions and without Yukawa couplings that the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect could be triggered by the light masses of fermions. This suggests that an explanation entirely within the Standard Model could be possible. item.description: We present a new class of 4-dimensional Grand Unified Theories where the gauge sectors of the standard model have a novel embedding in the unified group that does not factor through an $SU(5)$ subgroup. item.description: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration, Virgo Collaboration, and KAGRA Collaboration) Numerous well-motivated particle-physics-based models are constrained using the most recent LIGO-Virgo gravitational-wave data. [Phys. Rev. X 16, 041023] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026 — A. G. Abac et al. — Physical Review X

item.title: Standard Model of Electromagnetism and Chirality in Crystals
item.description: Author(s): R. Winkler and U. Zülicke A comprehensive symmetry-based classification identifies 12 fundamentally distinct types of crystal structures across five polar and five chiral categories, providing a complete taxonomy to predict and engineer next-generation multifunctional materials. [Phys. Rev. X 16, 031039] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026 — R. Winkler, U. Zülicke — Physical Review X
